</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Graph F1</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Given predicted graph <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G(V^{p},E^{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>E</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G(V^{p},E^{p})</annotation></semantics></math> and gold graph <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G(V^{g},E^{g})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>E</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G(V^{g},E^{g})</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute the Maximum Common Induced Subgraph (MCIS):</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A2.Ex5" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex5X"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex5X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle G_{mcis}(V_{mcis},E_{mcis})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle G_{mcis}(V_{mcis},E_{mcis})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex5X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\text{MCIS}\!\Big(G(V^{p},E^{p})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mpadded style="width:2.884em;" width="2.884em"><mtext>MCIS</mtext></mpadded><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>V</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>p</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>E</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>p</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\text{MCIS}\!\Big(G(V^{p},E^{p}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A2.Ex5Xa"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex5Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle G(V^{g},E^{g})\Big)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" rspace="4.560em">OPEN</mo><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>E</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle G(V^{g},E^{g})\Big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">If the largest matched subgraph contains <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=|V_{mcis}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=|V_{mcis}|</annotation></semantics></math> nodes, then</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A2.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\text{graph}}=\frac{k}{|V^{p}|},\qquad r_{\text{graph}}=\frac{k}{|V^{g}|}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>graph</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>p</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mtext>graph</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\text{graph}}=\frac{k}{|V^{p}|},\qquad r_{\text{graph}}=\frac{k}{|V^{g}|},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">and the final score is</p>
<table id="A2.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{1}^{\text{graph}}=\frac{2\,p_{\text{graph}}\,r_{\text{graph}}}{p_{\text{graph}}+r_{\text{graph}}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mn>1</mn><mtext>graph</mtext></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>graph</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mtext>graph</mtext></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>graph</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mtext>graph</mtext></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{1}^{\text{graph}}=\frac{2\,p_{\text{graph}}\,r_{\text{graph}}}{p_{\text{graph}}+r_{\text{graph}}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">This procedure captures both node correctness and edge consistency, providing a stricter evaluation than simple edge overlap.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>BLEU and GLEU</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">BLEU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Papineni et al. (2002)</a></cite> measures n-gram precision between candidate and gold step descriptions, with a brevity penalty to discourage very short outputs. GLEU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al. (2016)</a></cite> balances precision and recall over n-grams, making it more robust to short sequences. Both are computed at the step-text level and then averaged across workflows.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>BERTScore</h3>

<div id="A2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">BERTScore <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. (2020)</a></cite> computes similarity between candidate and gold step texts using contextual embeddings (we use <span id="A2.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">all-mpnet-base-v2</span>). For each candidate token, the maximum cosine similarity with gold tokens is taken, yielding precision, recall, and F1. Scores are averaged across workflow steps.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.5 </span>Kendall’s <math id="A2.SS5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math></h3>

<div id="A2.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Kendall’s <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kendall (1938)</a></cite> measures the ordinal correlation between two ranked lists. For workflows, we treat the step ordering as a ranking and compute</p>
<table id="A2.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=\frac{C-D}{\tfrac{1}{2}n(n-1)}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=\frac{C-D}{\tfrac{1}{2}n(n-1)},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of aligned steps being compared, and <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> denote the numbers of concordant and discordant step pairs, respectively. <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> ranges from <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> (complete disagreement) to <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> (perfect agreement).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.6 </span>LLM-as-Judge Prompts</h3>

<div id="A2.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the LLM-as-Judge evaluation, we designed a rubric-based prompt that instructs the model to compare a generated workflow against a gold reference.
Workflows are formatted with explicit node and edge lists.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.6.1 </span>Rubric</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A2.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">0 = Completely Incorrect or Irrelevant</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">1 = Major Flaws (breaks core logic)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">2 = Significant Issues (omits several key steps or adds wrong steps)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">3 = Noticeable Errors (minor reorder or one extra/missing non-critical step)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">4 = Very Good (only one minor step missing)</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">5 = Perfect Match (fully adheres, detailed, accurate)</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.6.2 </span>Anchor Examples</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide concrete anchors to calibrate the model’s scoring:</p>
<ul id="A2.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A2.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Example A (Score 4): Workflow missing one minor step.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Example B (Score 5): Workflow perfectly matches the gold.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Example C (Score 3): Workflow with minor reordering of steps.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Example D (Score 2): Workflow with extra irrelevant steps.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Example E (Score 0): Workflow completely incorrect relative to task.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.6.3 </span>Prompt Format</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The model is instructed to:</p>
<ol id="A2.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A2.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A2.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">List nodes and edges from both workflows.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A2.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Match nodes by content.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A2.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Identify missing, extra, or reordered steps.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A2.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Assign an initial score using the rubric.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I3.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="A2.I3.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I3.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Perform a self-check: confirm if the initial score strictly follows the rubric.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I3.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">6.</span> 
<div id="A2.I3.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I3.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Adjust to a final score if necessary.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS4" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.6.4 </span>Expected Output</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The model must return exactly one JSON object with the fields:</p><pre id="A2.SS6.SSS4.p1.2" class="ltx_verbatim ltx_font_typewriter">
{
  "ThoughtChain": "&lt;step-by-step reasoning&gt;",
  "initial_score": &lt;int 0–5&gt;,
  "self_check": {
    "consistent": "Yes"|"No",
    "final_score": &lt;int 0–5&gt;
  },
  "justification": "&lt;one-sentence summary&gt;"
}
</pre>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS5" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">B.6.5 </span>Implementation Notes</h4>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use GPT-4o via Azure OpenAI with temperature 0.0 to minimize randomness.
Each workflow pair is evaluated across multiple prompt templates, and scores are averaged to reduce variance.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>

<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Sensitivity Analysis</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To quantify how rapidly each metric’s score degrades as perturbation severity increases, we define the <span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">sensitivity</span> of metric <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> to leverage all available perturbation levels:</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A3.E1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="A3.E1X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E1X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\Delta_{m}^{\text{avg}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>m</mi><mtext>avg</mtext></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\Delta_{m}^{\text{avg}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E1X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\Bigg[\frac{\bar{s}_{m}(10\%)-\bar{s}_{m}(30\%)}{0.20}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo maxsize="2.600em" minsize="2.600em">[</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mn>0.20</mn></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\Bigg[\frac{\bar{s}_{m}(10\%)-\bar{s}_{m}(30\%)}{0.20}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A3.E1Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E1Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle+\frac{\bar{s}_{m}(30\%)-\bar{s}_{m}(50\%)}{0.20}\Bigg]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>30</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mn>0.20</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo maxsize="2.600em" minsize="2.600em">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle+\frac{\bar{s}_{m}(30\%)-\bar{s}_{m}(50\%)}{0.20}\Bigg]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{s}_{m}(\alpha)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>s</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{s}_{m}(\alpha)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the mean score of metric <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> at <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>% perturbation (see Tables <a href="#A3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Appendix C Results Discussion ‣ WorkflowPerturb: Calibrated Stress Tests for Evaluating Multi-Agent Workflow Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, <a href="#A3.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Appendix C Results Discussion ‣ WorkflowPerturb: Calibrated Stress Tests for Evaluating Multi-Agent Workflow Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, <a href="#A3.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Appendix C Results Discussion ‣ WorkflowPerturb: Calibrated Stress Tests for Evaluating Multi-Agent Workflow Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).
This formulation averages the degradation rates across both the 10<math id="A3.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math>30% and 30<math id="A3.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math>50% intervals, providing a more stable and representative estimate of how sensitively each metric responds to perturbations.
By considering multiple intervals, <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{m}^{\text{avg}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>m</mi><mtext>avg</mtext></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{m}^{\text{avg}}</annotation></semantics></math> mitigates the effect of local non-linearities or noise and yields a smoother measure of robustness.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F6" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17990v1/sensitivity.svg" id="A3.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/238;" width="476" height="238"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>Metric sensitivity across perturbation types (mean <math id="A3.F6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> std) for Description Change.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A3.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ C.1 Sensitivity Analysis ‣ Appendix C Results Discussion ‣ WorkflowPerturb: Calibrated Stress Tests for Evaluating Multi-Agent Workflow Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> visualizes <math id="A3.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{m}^{\mathrm{avg}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>avg</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{m}^{\mathrm{avg}}</annotation></semantics></math> across three perturbation types, namely <span id="A3.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Removed Steps</span>, <span id="A3.SS1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Compressed Steps</span>, and <span id="A3.SS1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Description Edits</span>, for all seven metrics.
Several consistent patterns emerge:</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Structural metrics (Graph F1, Chain F1).</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Both Graph F1 and Chain F1 show their highest sensitivity under <em id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">compressed steps</em>, with <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{m}^{\mathrm{avg}}\!=\!1.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>avg</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0.108em">=</mo><mn>1.03</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{m}^{\mathrm{avg}}\!=\!1.03</annotation></semantics></math> in Figure <a href="#A3.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ C.1 Sensitivity Analysis ‣ Appendix C Results Discussion ‣ WorkflowPerturb: Calibrated Stress Tests for Evaluating Multi-Agent Workflow Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, indicating that node merging disrupts edges and paths more than equivalent rates of removal. Sensitivity under <em id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">removed steps</em> is moderate (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.73" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.73</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.73</annotation></semantics></math>), while <em id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">description edits</em> remain low (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.30</annotation></semantics></math>), consistent with topology being unchanged. The two metrics follow nearly identical patterns across perturbation types, peaking for compression, lower for removal, and minimal for description edits, confirming that both primarily capture structural distortions rather than surface-level rewording.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Lexical metrics (BLEU, GLEU)</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">BLEU and GLEU show generally high sensitivity (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{m}^{\mathrm{avg}}\!\approx\!0.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>avg</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0.108em">≈</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{m}^{\mathrm{avg}}\!\approx\!0.8</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.25</annotation></semantics></math>).
Both peak for <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Removed Steps</span> (BLEU <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=1.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>1.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=1.25</annotation></semantics></math>, GLEU <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=0.95</annotation></semantics></math>), indicating that token loss and reordering drive the strongest drops.
Under <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Compressed Steps</span>, sensitivity is lower but still substantial (BLEU = 0.90<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext=",GLEU=0.83" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>G</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>U</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.83</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">,GLEU=0.83</annotation></semantics></math>).
For <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Description Edits</span>, BLEU remains high yet slightly below compression (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.88" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.88</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.88</annotation></semantics></math>), while GLEU is roughly on par with—or a touch above, compression (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.85" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.85</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.85</annotation></semantics></math>).
Overall, removals cause the greatest lexical disruption; compression and paraphrasing are both detected, with BLEU slightly more affected by compression and GLEU slightly more responsive to paraphrasing.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Embedding metrics (BERTScore).</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">BERTScore shows comparatively low sensitivity overall (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{m}^{\mathrm{avg}}&lt;0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>avg</mi></msubsup><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{m}^{\mathrm{avg}}&lt;0.4</annotation></semantics></math>), indicating tolerance to moderate structural or lexical changes.
It remains low for <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Removed</span> and <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Compressed</span> cases (each <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.23" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.23</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.23</annotation></semantics></math>) and rises only under <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Description Edits</span> (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.38" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.38</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.38</annotation></semantics></math>), reflecting resilience to paraphrasing with some sensitivity to semantic drift.
The generally low magnitudes suggest limited discriminative power across perturbation severities: BERTScore tends to group mild and severe variants more closely than structural or lexical metrics.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Order-based metric (Kendall’s <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>).</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Kendall’s <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> is strongest for <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Compressed Steps</span> (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.43" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.43</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.43</annotation></semantics></math>), indicating that merging nodes substantially alters pairwise precedence relations.
Sensitivity for <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Removed Steps</span> is lower but still high (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.93" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.93</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.93</annotation></semantics></math>), reflecting order disruptions from deleting intermediate steps.
For <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Description Edits</span>, sensitivity is near zero (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.03</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.03</annotation></semantics></math>), consistent with unchanged topology.
Overall, Kendall’s <math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> reliably captures order-level distortions, peaking when compression collapses or reshuffles task sequences.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Judgment-based metric (LLM–as–Judge).</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">LLM–as–Judge shows high sensitivity for <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Removed Steps</span> (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.99" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.99</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.99</annotation></semantics></math>) and substantial sensitivity for <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Compressed Steps</span> (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.87" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.87</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.87</annotation></semantics></math>), while remaining nearly flat for <span id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Description Edits</span> (<math id="A3.SS1.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.03</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.03</annotation></semantics></math>).
This pattern indicates that the judgment signal prioritizes functional completeness and procedural detail, reliably flagging structural loss but largely ignoring wording changes when topology is intact.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
</article>
</div>
